Background The effects of a multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) on markers of inflammation and muscle damage, perceived soreness and lower limb performance are unknown in endurance-trained female athletes. The purpose of this study was to determine the impact of MIPS (NO-Shotgun®) pre-loaded 4 weeks prior to a single-bout of downhill running (DHR) on hsC-Reactive Protein (hsCRP), interleukin (IL)-6, creatine kinase (CK), muscle soreness, lower limb circumferences and performance. Method Trained female runners ( n = 8; 29 ± 5.9 years) (VO 2max : ≥ 50 ml -1 .kg -1 .min -1 , midfollicular phase (7-11 days post-menses) were randomly assigned in a double-blind manner into two groups: MIPS ( n = 4) ingested one serving of NO Shotgun daily for 28 days prior to DHR and 30 min prior to all post-testing visits; Control (CON) ( n = 4) consumed an isocaloric maltodextrin placebo in an identical manner to MIPS. hsCRP, IL-6, CK, perceived soreness, limb circumferences, and performance measures (flexibility, squat jump peak power) were tested on 5 occasions; immediately before (PRE), immediately post-DHR, 24, 48 and 72 h post-DHR. Results There were main effects of time for CK ( p = 0.05), pain pressure threshold (right tibialis anterior ( p = 0.010), right biceps femoris ( p = 0.01), and left iliotibial band (ITB) ( p = 0.05) across all time points), and maximum squat jump power ( p = 0.04). Compared with 24 h post-DHR, maximum squat jump power was significantly lower at 48 h post-DHR ( p = 0.05). Lower body perceived soreness was significantly increased at 24 h ( p = 0.02) and baseline to 48 h ( p = 0.02) post DHR. IL-6 peaked immediately post-DHR ( p = 0.03) and hsCRP peaked at 24 h post-DHR ( p = 0.06). Calculation of effect sizes indicated a moderate attenuation of hsCRP in MIPS at 72 h post-DHR. Conclusions Consumption of MIPS for 4 weeks prior to a single bout of DHR attenuated inflammation three days post, but did not affect perceived soreness and muscle damage markers in endurance trained female runners following a single bout of DHR. Keywords Eccentric exercise Muscle soreness Recovery issue-copyright-statement © The Author(s) 2016 Background Exhaustive or unaccustomed high-intensity exercise [ 1 , 2 ] or eccentric contractions [ 3 , 4 ] are known to inflict muscle damage. This leads to increased muscle soreness, decreased muscle strength, increased concentration of plasma muscle enzymes, and decreased range of motion [ 1 , 2 , 4 ], for several days post exercise, and further promotes an unbalanced ratio of protein breakdown to protein synthesis [ 5 ]. A level of muscle discomfort related to the exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), otherwise known as delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS), increases until subsiding five to seven days post-exercise [ 6 ]. Downhill running (DHR) is commonly used to induce muscle damage [ 7 ], as it involves greater eccentric contraction of the knee extensors, leading to more tissue damage, compared with level or uphill running [ 8 , 9 ]. Although similar decrements associated with EIMD have been reported in both males and females, it has been documented that females are susceptible to longer periods of recovery when compared to males; however, reasons for this are unclear [ 10 ]. However, contrary to this, estrogen appears to have a protective effect with regards to DOMS [ 11 ], as it has been reported that estrogen results in significant decreases in serum creatine kinase (CK) activities post-exercise or post-injury when compare to men or a placebo [ 12 , 13 ]. It has therefore been hypothesized that several of the sex-related differences are attributed to the female sex hormone 17β-estradiol [ 14 , 15 ]; such that estrogen has been reported to possess the ability to enhance skeletal muscle growth, gene expression, metabolism, contraction characteristics, and maintain muscle mass. Numerous studies have examined the effects of nutritional supplementation interventions to reduce the effects of EIMD by increasing the net protein balance within skeletal muscle. These studies have included supplementation with whey protein isolate [ 5 , 16 ], branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs: leucine, isoleucine, and valine) [ 17 , 18 ], protein hydrolysates [ 19 ], leucine only [ 20 ], creatine [ 21 ]; increasing anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant activity through tart cherry juice [ 22 , 23 ], blueberry [ 24 ] and caffeine ingestion [ 25 ], as well as enhancing recovery through the consumption of chocolate milk [ 26 , 27 ] to name a few. The majority of studies investigating the ergogenic effects of nutritional supplementation on exercise performance and recovery have primarily focused on males [ 20 , 28 , 29 ]. However, there are a few studies that examined female rats and other animals, and female humans [ 30 , 31 ]. Recent studies have investigated the effects of a multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS; NO Shotgun®) following a single bout of DHR in trained males [ 32 ] as well as in resistance trained males [ 33 ]. However, there is little known about the effects of this MIPS on the reduction of muscle damage and repair after EIMD from DHR in endurance-trained female athletes. We hypothesized that 4 weeks of pre-loading with a MIPS prior to a single bout of DHR would decrease perceived soreness and circumferences, enhance flexibility, and improve biochemical markers of muscle damage and inflammation (i.e. CK, IL-6 and CRP), and improve squat jump performance when compared to an isocaloric placebo (CON) in endurance-trained female runners for up to 72 h post-DHR.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the effects of 4-weeks of multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) pre-loading on markers of inflammation (hsCRP, IL-6), muscle damage (CK), perceived muscle soreness, tissue tenderness, and lower limb performance (squat jump peak power, hamstring flexibility) in endurance-trained female runners after a single bout of downhill running (DHR). MIPS consumption attenuated inflammation (hsCRP) three days post-DHR but did not significantly impact perceived soreness, muscle damage markers, or other performance measures.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS, NO-Shotgun®) and eccentric exercise (Downhill Running, DHR).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: MIPS (NO-Shotgun®) was consumed daily for 28 days (4 weeks) prior to a single bout of DHR, and 30 minutes before post-testing. One serving of MIPS was 21g. A control group received an isocaloric (28g maltodextrin) placebo. The DHR protocol involved a 60-minute run at a -10% gradient, at 75% VO2max (average speed 12.03  ± 0.4 km/hr). No dose-response comparisons for either the supplement or DHR protocol were reported.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Elevated initially, then attenuated in MIPS group.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peaked at 24 h post-DHR (p = 0.06). A significant decrease was observed between 24 and 48 h post-DHR (p=0.04). At 72 h post-DHR, the MIPS group showed a moderate attenuation/decrease (-38.89% of baseline) compared to the CON group which showed a moderate increase and remained above baseline.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A general marker of systemic inflammation and an acute-phase reactant, stimulated by pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates systemic inflammatory response to exercise-induced muscle damage; attenuation suggests a reduced inflammatory response, while an increase signifies an inflammatory response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peaked immediately post-DHR (p = 0.03), with a significant 62.99% increase. Levels remained elevated up to 72 h post-DHR. No significant difference was reported between MIPS and placebo groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune response, muscle repair, and stimulating hepatic CRP production.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates inflammatory response to exercise-induced muscle damage and its activation in muscle repair processes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed main effects of time (p = 0.05), with a significant increase from baseline to immediately post-DHR (p=0.02) and peak increases at 24 h post-DHR. MIPS consumption did not significantly affect CK levels compared to placebo.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An enzyme released from damaged muscle cells, widely used as an indicator of muscle injury and cellular integrity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage and the recovery status following strenuous eccentric exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Subjective self-report (lower body) via Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and pressure algometer.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Lower body perceived soreness significantly increased at 24 h (p=0.02) and 48 h (p=0.02) post-DHR, showing 5-6 fold increases from baseline. Peak soreness and tenderness occurred at 24-48 h post-DHR. MIPS consumption did not significantly affect perceived soreness.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Subjective sensation of muscle pain and tenderness resulting from micro-trauma to muscle fibers during unaccustomed or strenuous eccentric exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level and severity of exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) and discomfort, impacting recovery and subsequent performance.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Various lower limb muscles and fascia (e.g., right tibialis anterior, right biceps femoris, left iliotibial band, hip flexors).
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Pain Sensitivity / Pressure Tolerance (Algometer force measurement)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant time effects were observed for right tibialis anterior (p=0.01), right biceps femoris (p=0.01), and left ITB (p=0.05) across all time points, indicating increased tenderness. Peak decrement was observed at 24 h post-DHR. MIPS consumption did not significantly attenuate these changes.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An objective measure of tissue tenderness and pain sensitivity, reflecting local muscle damage and inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates localized exercise-induced muscle damage and soreness, contributing to reduced functional capacity and discomfort.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Showed main effects of time (p = 0.04), with peak decrements at 48 h post-DHR, being significantly lower than at 24 h post-DHR (p=0.05). MIPS did not significantly attenuate these decrements compared to placebo.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An indicator of muscle contractile function, explosive strength, and neuromuscular efficiency.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Measured following a single bout of strenuous downhill running (DHR) in endurance-trained female runners, with 4 weeks of MIPS pre-loading or placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired muscle function and recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage, affecting athletic performance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant change was observed in hamstring flexibility following the DHR in both MIPS and CON groups. MIPS did not elicit significant improvements.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: The extensibility of hamstring muscles and the range of motion at the hip joint.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Following a single bout of strenuous Downhill Running (DHR) in well-trained female endurance runners, with MIPS supplementation versus placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates muscle stiffness or impaired range of motion. In this study, despite pain, flexibility was not significantly compromised in hamstrings.
